# Unit-of-work and data-access boundaries

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `ef-context-concurrency` · **EF Core & LINQ** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S01-Q039](#S01-Q039)

<p>Explain Repository, Generic Repository and Unit of Work through one data-changing use case. Which responsibility belongs to each abstraction?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Define a data-changing unit of work and defend its context, conflict and abstraction boundaries.</p>

<ul>
<li>Trace DbContext lifetime and the consistency boundary.</li>
<li>Specify optimistic-conflict behavior and evidence for retry or rejection.</li>
<li>Justify repository abstractions or raw SQL from a concrete requirement.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [LINQ execution and result cardinality](ef-query-execution.md)

<p>First identify the changes that belong together and who owns their lifetime. Concurrency tests whether that operation still makes sense when another writer intervenes; repository and query choices are then judged by whether they express the same contract clearly.</p>

<a id="S01-Q039"></a>

### S01-Q039 · Foundation

<p>Explain Repository, Generic Repository and Unit of Work through one data-changing use case. Which responsibility belongs to each abstraction?</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q039](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q039)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q039](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q039)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain Repository Pattern, Generic Repository Pattern, and Unit of Work.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace retrieval, changes and the intended consistency boundary. A generic abstraction uses a shared shape across entities; assess what that shape does and does not express.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain data-access responsibilities without conflating patterns.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a hypothetical operation over related data; state transaction expectations and keep the conceptual patterns distinct from provider-specific implementation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces the operation and makes the commit or consistency boundary explicit.</li>
<li>Explains where a uniform abstraction fits or obscures entity-specific requirements.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Describing all three as interchangeable wrappers around CRUD.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would the design express an operation that changes two related entities together?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q034"></a>

### S02-Q034 · Mechanism

<p>How would you manage DbContext lifetime for a web application and its units of work?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q034](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q034)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q034](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q034)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How should `DbContext` lifetime be managed in a web application?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A unit of work is the boundary of related data operations intended to be managed together. Explain ownership, disposal and concurrent use in a concrete request or background operation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Align context ownership with work boundaries and concurrency requirements.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State EF Core version, DI registration and any pooling or factory use; consult official lifetime and concurrency documentation before asserting guarantees.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace who creates, uses and disposes the context in one operation.</li>
<li>Explain a concurrent-use or long-running-work risk and how to test the chosen boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating a single shared context as a universal cache or assuming request scope automatically fits every job.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What changes for work that continues after the request finishes?</li>
<li>How would parallel data operations affect your context ownership?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q033"></a>

### S02-Q033 · Failure cases

<p>How would optimistic concurrency detect conflicting updates, and what role could a row-version token play?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q033](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q033)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q033](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q033)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain optimistic concurrency and row-version based conflict detection.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Optimistic concurrency detects whether assumptions from an earlier read still hold at write time. Explain how the application should interpret and resolve a conflict, not just name a token.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Protect a business update by detecting and handling stale-write conflicts.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State EF Core version, provider and token configuration; distinguish SQL Server rowversion from a generic application token and check official semantics.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace two readers and competing writes, identifying the conflict boundary.</li>
<li>Define a business-appropriate resolution policy and a concurrent-update test.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Calling rowversion a wall-clock timestamp or retrying a business conflict without re-evaluating the data.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which updates could you merge, and which require the caller to decide?</li>
<li>How would you preserve the original user intent after reloading current data?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q035 · Trade-offs

<p>When would raw SQL or a stored procedure be justified instead of LINQ for one data operation?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q035](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q035)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q035](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q035)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When is raw SQL or a stored procedure justified instead of LINQ?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Choose from a concrete capability or measured limitation, then account for the resulting maintenance and correctness obligations. Compare alternatives without assuming handwritten SQL is inherently faster.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Justify a data-access boundary with requirements and verifiable trade-offs.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name EF Core version, provider and operation; check official parameterization, result mapping and tracking behavior for the chosen API.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Show the requirement or evidence that LINQ does not meet well.</li>
<li>Compare parameter safety, transaction ownership, mapping and regression checks.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Choosing raw SQL solely for a presumed speed advantage or concatenating untrusted input into SQL text.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What evidence would let you return to a LINQ implementation?</li>
<li>How would you test schema changes against the chosen result mapping?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S01-Q040"></a>

### S01-Q040 · Trade-offs

<p>With EF Core already handling data access and change coordination, when would an additional repository abstraction help? When would you leave it out?</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q040](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q040)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q040](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q040)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> EF Core already implements repository/unit-of-work-like behavior. When does an additional repository abstraction help, and when does it add unnecessary complexity?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Assess the requirements served by the extra boundary. Compare meaningful encapsulation with duplication or lost query expressiveness, rather than prescribing a pattern universally.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Justify an abstraction from requirements and measurable design consequences.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name EF Core and provider versions; check official documentation for the capabilities the comparison depends on and state the use case being encapsulated.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Shows the capability added by the abstraction and the caller it protects.</li>
<li>Compares the simpler option and a realistic testing or query requirement.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming a repository is mandatory for testability or useless in every EF Core application.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would your abstraction support a specialized query without leaking every provider detail?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Two hypothetical requests edit the same record through EF Core. Define each unit of work, propose how a conflicting update is detected and surfaced, then compare direct EF usage with an extra repository for a specialized query. State provider/version assumptions and design a concurrent-writer check without claiming it has run.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains context ownership, a conflict and the responsibilities of repository/unit-of-work patterns.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends user-visible conflict handling and the extra abstraction or SQL choice with targeted checks.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A CRUD wrapper or a retry instruction alone does not establish transaction or conflict correctness.</p>
